# Unlimited v1.0 — protocol examples

Generated by `make docs` from the library code (`tools/doc_examples.cpp`); do not edit by hand. Every number below comes from the library function named with it, and every example that `spec.md` also gives is checked against the library: `make docs` stops when they disagree. Section numbers in parentheses refer to `spec.md`.

## 1. Speeds (spec 1.3)

The speed B is given in bytes per second, the same on both sides; T = 1 / (10 B) is `slot_us_for_speed(B)`, rounded to the microsecond. Every byte is one window of 10 slots, so the net rate is exactly B bytes/s (8 B bit/s). The occupied band (99 % of the power) is `occupied_band(1500, T)`; the −26 dB and −40 dB widths are `width_26db_hz(T)` and `width_40db_hz(T)`; the shift tolerance is `passband_fit(config)` in the 2.4 kHz SSB filter (300–2700 Hz): how far the pitch may move down / up and still pass the filter and be found by the receiver of that speed. The look-ahead is `Decoder::lookahead_samples()`: the receiver's events come this much after the audio (spec 3.1).

| Speed | T | Samples per slot at 8 kHz | Bit rate | Occupied band | −26 dB width | −40 dB width | Shift tolerance (300–2700 Hz) | Look-ahead | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1.00 bytes/s** | 100.000 ms | 800.00 | 8 bit/s | 44 Hz, 1478–1522 Hz | 70 Hz | 99 Hz | ±1178 Hz | 3200 samples = 400 ms | very weak HF paths |
| **3.00 bytes/s** | 33.333 ms | 266.66 | 24 bit/s | 134 Hz, 1433–1567 Hz | 211 Hz | 298 Hz | ±1133 Hz | 2133 samples = 267 ms | weak HF |
| **6.00 bytes/s** | 16.667 ms | 133.34 | 48 bit/s | 264 Hz, 1368–1632 Hz | 420 Hz | 594 Hz | ±1068 Hz | 1866 samples = 233 ms | HF default |
| **12.00 bytes/s** | 8.333 ms | 66.66 | 96 bit/s | 530 Hz, 1235–1765 Hz | 841 Hz | 1189 Hz | ±935 Hz | 1733 samples = 217 ms | good HF, AM |
| **25.00 bytes/s** | 4.000 ms | 32.00 | 200 bit/s | 1100 Hz, 950–2050 Hz | 1750 Hz | 2475 Hz | ±650 Hz | 1664 samples = 208 ms | FM |

Any speed from 1.00 to 25.00 bytes/s in steps of 0.01 is valid (`slot_valid()`); `centi_bytes_per_second()` and `slot_us_for_centi_speed()` are the integer forms for the AVR.

## 2. "Hi" = 0x48 0x69 at 6 bytes/s, slot by slot (spec 2.2)

`EncoderConfig()` (6 bytes/s: T 16.667 ms, 1500 Hz, 8000 Hz, no lead-in, 100 ms tail). Each byte is one window: START, its 8 bits most significant first (a beep is 1, silence is 0), STOP. Windows follow each other with no gap. Read from `Encoder::status()` at the first sample of each slot; slot j starts at sample ceil(j × 133.336).

| Window | Slots 0..9 (T = tone, . = silence) | Byte |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `T . T . . T . . . T` | 0x48 'H' = 0100 1000 |
| 1 | `T . T T . T . . T T` | 0x69 'i' = 0110 1001 |

The transmission: 20 slots = 333 ms of signal and the tail, 3467 samples = 433.4 ms in all (`duration_samples(2)`). A key pressed alone is one window: 167 ms at 6 bytes/s.

## 3. With a VOX lead (spec 2.1)

`vox_lead_ms` 150 at 6 bytes/s: a steady tone of max(ceil(150 ms / T), 3) = 9 slots, ramped up in its first slot and down in its last, then 2 silent slots; the START of byte 0 is the first tone after them, at 183.4 ms. "Hi" then takes 4934 samples = 616.8 ms. A lead shorter than 3 slots is stretched: the receiver tells a steady tone from beeps by its first two slot boundaries, where beeps fall silent.

## 4. Airtime (spec 2.4)

`duration_samples(n)` / 8000 for n bytes: lead-in + (VOX lead + gap + 10 n) T + max(tail, 2 T), with no lead-in and the 100 ms tail; the same with a 150 ms VOX lead in brackets.

| Speed | 1 byte | 10 bytes | 100 bytes | 1000 bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.00 bytes/s | 1.20 s (1.70 s) | 10.20 s (10.70 s) | 100.20 s (100.70 s) | 1000.20 s (1000.70 s) |
| 3.00 bytes/s | 0.43 s (0.67 s) | 3.43 s (3.67 s) | 33.43 s (33.67 s) | 333.43 s (333.66 s) |
| 6.00 bytes/s | 0.27 s (0.45 s) | 1.77 s (1.95 s) | 16.77 s (16.95 s) | 166.77 s (166.95 s) |
| 12.00 bytes/s | 0.18 s (0.36 s) | 0.93 s (1.11 s) | 8.43 s (8.61 s) | 83.43 s (83.61 s) |
| 25.00 bytes/s | 0.14 s (0.30 s) | 0.50 s (0.66 s) | 4.10 s (4.26 s) | 40.10 s (40.26 s) |

100 bytes at 6 bytes/s are 16.7 s of windows (spec 2.4).

## 5. The signal in typical receiver filters (spec 1.3)

Pitch 1500 Hz. Each cell is the shift tolerance `passband_fit(config)` with the filter as `config.passband`: how far the pitch may move down / up (mistuning) and still pass the filter and be found by the receiver, whose search never leaves 300..2700 Hz. A signal that does not fit is refused by `EncoderConfig::check()` (`ConfigError::outside_passband`).

| Speed | 1.8 kHz SSB, 300–2100 Hz | 2.4 kHz SSB (default), 300–2700 Hz | 2.7 kHz SSB, 200–2900 Hz | AM, 100–3000 Hz | NBFM, 300–3000 Hz |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.00 bytes/s | −1178 / +578 Hz | ±1178 Hz | ±1200 Hz | ±1200 Hz | −1178 / +1200 Hz |
| 3.00 bytes/s | −1133 / +533 Hz | ±1133 Hz | ±1200 Hz | ±1200 Hz | −1133 / +1200 Hz |
| 6.00 bytes/s | −1068 / +468 Hz | ±1068 Hz | −1168 / +1200 Hz | ±1200 Hz | −1068 / +1200 Hz |
| 12.00 bytes/s | −935 / +335 Hz | ±935 Hz | −1035 / +1135 Hz | −1135 / +1200 Hz | −935 / +1200 Hz |
| 25.00 bytes/s | −650 / +50 Hz | ±650 Hz | −750 / +850 Hz | −850 / +950 Hz | −650 / +950 Hz |

## 6. The receiver's settings (spec 3, 5)

`DecoderConfig()`: 6.00 bytes/s, passband 300–2700 Hz, the adaptive decision line (`--threshold auto`, the default since 2026-09-28); the fixed line sits at `threshold_percent` (70 % by default) of each window's START–STOP reference line; impulse blanker on; fade bridge off (V16). The receiver searches the pitch in `search_range()`: the passband less half the occupied band at its speed, within 300..2700 Hz.

One byte, one decision (V20): the first window after the anchor is decided alone, like every other, and its byte comes out with `locked`; `dcd()` is on while the receiver tracks (spec 3.10).
